All 18 evidence records have been successfully extracted, recorded, and finalized from the IMF 2022 Article IV report (MAC-010) for the chapter 5B (Economic Wellbeing) assessment of Mexico under the AMLO administration for 2022.

## Summary of Completed Evidence Extraction

**Source**: IMF 2022 Article IV Consultation with Mexico (MAC-010)  
**Locators processed**: page 45, page 46, page 47, page 48  
**Total records**: 18 evidence intents across questions 5B.1–5B.10

### Records by Question Lens:

| Question | Evidence IDs | Content |
|----------|-------------|---------|
| 5B.3 (Fiscal rules) | D0003, D0004, D0012, D0014 | Fiscal balance, public debt, banking NPLs, debt servicing |
| 5B.4 (Fair competition) | D0010, D0011, D0013, D0014, D0018 | Banking resilience, credit growth, corporate leverage |
| 5B.5 (Anti-corruption) | D0011, D0012, D0018 | Development bank issues, financial credit |

| 5B.10 (Durable trajectory) | D0001, D0002, D0004, D0008, D0015, D0017 | GDP, expenditure, debt, poverty, social indicators |

### Key Observable Facts Extracted:
- GDP growth: +2.2% (2018), -0.2% (2019), -8.1% (2020), +4.8% (2021), +2.1% (2022 proj.)
- Fiscal deficit: -2.2% GDP (2018) worsening to -4.4% (2020), recovering to -3.8% (2022)
- Public debt: 53.6% GDP (2018), peaked at 60.1% (2020), 56.2% (2022 proj.)
- Poverty headcount: 43.9% (2020, CONEVAL multi-dimensional measure)
- Unemployment: 3.3% (2018) rising to 4.4% (2020), recovering to 3.4% (2022)
- Consumer inflation: 4.8% (2018) to 8.5% (2022)
- Financial system credit to private sector: recovering from 1.5% (2020) to 10.7% (2022)
